cubes.name: AssetCategories
cubes.title: Asset Categories
cubes.description: Lookup table of all asset type label. Type classify assets by type using snake_case IDs mapped to human-readable names - cloud (e.g., "virtual_machine" -> "Virtual Machine", "cloud_firewall" -> "Cloud Firewall", "dns_server" -> "DNS Server", "storage_bucket" -> "Storage Bucket"), network (e.g., "router" -> "Router", "switch" -> "Switch", "load_balancer" -> "Load Balancer"), and IoT/endpoint (e.g., "camera" -> "Camera", "printer" -> "Printer", "bare_metal_server" -> "Bare-Metal Server"). An asset can have multiple Types. Use this cube to list available categories and their display names. Example queries: "what types exist", "list all asset types", "show me all firewall assets", "how many virtual machines do I have", or populating a type filter dropdown.

cubes.name: AssetDetailsOnly
cubes.title: Asset Details Only
cubes.description: Asset-only inventory cube with one row per unique asset (no insight row expansion). Exposes common normalised asset attributes such as name, provider, region/location, OS/version, vendor/model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, taxonomy hierarchy, tags, lifecycle fields, and discovery status signals. Use this cube only for tag-introspection or asset-registry-lookup queries that do not enumerate assets by attribute, for example "find assets by tag key/value", "list all available tag keys", "count assets by provider", or "show devices by taxonomy type". Do NOT use this cube for general asset enumeration such as "list Windows servers", "show managed devices by region", or "find assets by OS" — use AssetDetails_ch_agg for those. Do NOT use this cube when the query requires insight-specific fields (indicator/state/severity/confidence) or provider/interface expanded raw attributes; use AssetDetails_ch_agg in that case. Time dimension: default to updated_at scoped to the last 7 days from now (to the minute); if the user specifies a time range — for example "in the last 3 hours", "over the past 2 days", or "not in the last 3 days" — apply those constraints instead, as user-specified time always takes priority over the default.

cubes.name: AssetDetails_ch
cubes.title: Asset Details Ch
cubes.description: Primary detail asset-and-insight cube combining normalised asset attributes, active insight rows, and 7-day user logon counts. Grain is one row per asset-insight combination, so a single asset can produce multiple rows when it has multiple active insights. Each row exposes: (1) common asset context such as provider, region, OS, vendor, model, categories, taxonomy, tags, lifecycle timestamps, and discovery status fields; (2) one active insight record with classification, indicator, rule ID, confidence, severity, state, and sub-classification; and (3) asset-level recent user activity counts. Use this cube when a query needs both asset context and per-insight detail, for example "show active insights by provider and severity", "list assets with registration issues by region", or "break down violated insights by taxonomy type and confidence". This cube and AssetInsightOnly both have one insight per row, so both can correctly GROUP BY or break down by insight dimensions (classification, sub-classification, indicator, confidence, severity, state); prefer this cube when the breakdown also groups by or returns asset attributes (provider, OS, region, vendor, taxonomy), and prefer AssetInsightOnly for lightweight insight-only breakdowns with little or no asset context. For asset inventory with rolled-up insight arrays — one row per asset, insight fields used only for filtering — prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg; do NOT use AssetDetails_ch_agg to group by an insight dimension, as its insight fields are per-asset arrays. Time dimension: default to updated_at scoped to the last 7 days from now (to the minute); if the user specifies a time range — for example "in the last 3 hours", "over the past 2 days", or "not in the last 3 days" — apply those constraints instead, as user-specified time always takes priority over the default.

cubes.name: AssetDetails_ch_agg
cubes.title: Asset Details Ch Agg
cubes.description: Primary aggregated asset cube combining normalised asset attributes, rolled-up insight arrays, and 7-day user logon summaries. Grain is one row per asset (CQID). Each row exposes: (1) common asset fields - name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insight context - insight types, indicators, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys such as insight_types_confidence_levels; and (3) user activity rollups - distinct user count plus user-to-name/action/timestamp maps. This is the default workhorse cube for all general asset queries — use it with or without insight filtering. Use for any asset enumeration or attribute-based lookup, for example "list all Windows servers", "show all managed Linux devices by region", "list managed assets by OS and vendor", "find assets by name or IP", as well as insight-filtered analytics such as "show assets with active security insights by OS" or "list devices with recent user activity and violations". Insight fields here (classification, sub-classification, indicator, confidence, severity, state) are stored as per-asset arrays: use them to FILTER assets that have a given insight, but NOT to GROUP or break down BY an insight value — grouping operates on the whole array, not individual values, and produces incorrect counts. For any query that groups by, breaks down by, or counts WITHIN an insight dimension (e.g. "zombie assets by sub-classification", "count insights by severity", "breakdown by classification and confidence"), use AssetInsightOnly (pure insight breakdown, minimal asset context) or AssetDetails_ch (one row per asset-insight, when the breakdown also groups by or returns asset attributes such as provider, OS, region, or vendor) instead. For interface- or provider-specific raw fields, use the corresponding *_agg_expanded cubes. Time dimension: default to updated_at scoped to the last 7 days from now (to the minute); if the user specifies a time range — for example "in the last 3 hours", "over the past 2 days", or "not in the last 3 days" — apply those constraints instead, as user-specified time always takes priority over the default.

cubes.name: AssetDiscoveryStatus
cubes.title: Asset Discovery Status
cubes.description: Device discovery-status cube with one row per asset. Exposes discovery and network collection health fields such as device IP/name/type, reachability results, SNMP or CLI or SDN credential and collection statuses, fingerprinting outcomes, discovery timestamps, overall status, discovery service identifiers, and device-type confidence signals. Use this cube when a query focuses on operational discovery health rather than general asset inventory or insight analytics, for example "show unreachable devices by type", "list assets with failed SNMP credentials", "find devices with low type-identification confidence", or "track SDN collection failures by source job". Prefer this cube over broader asset cube when the question is primarily about discovery workflow status because it keeps the surface focused on discovery-specific fields.

cubes.name: AssetInsight
cubes.title: Asset Insight
cubes.description: Security and compliance insight cube enriched with dictionary labels for insight type, indicator, and location. Grain is detailed and time-aware: rows represent indicator/rule findings per asset over time windows, with latest values selected per grouped keys in the query logic. Use this cube for insight-centric analysis such as "show active violations by severity", "list findings by indicator and provider", "track acknowledged vs unacknowledged insights", or "break down insights by asset type/location". Prefer this cube when the question is primarily about insight lifecycle, confidence, severity, and violation state. Do NOT use this cube for broad asset inventory fields (tags, reconciliation, interface details, provider raw JSON).

cubes.name: AssetInsightOnly
cubes.title: Asset Insight Only
cubes.description: Insight-only cube combining active insight rows with minimal asset status context. Grain is one row per active insight per asset, so a single asset can produce multiple rows when it has multiple active findings. Each row exposes the per-insight fields needed for security analysis, including classification, indicator, rule ID, state, confidence, severity, sub-classification, and sync timestamps, plus managed status for basic asset scoping. Use this cube when the question is about insight behaviour itself rather than broader asset inventory, for example "show active insights by severity", "count registration findings by confidence", or "list assets with a specific indicator rule". Choose this cube or AssetDetails_ch over AssetDetails_ch_agg whenever the query groups by, breaks down by, or counts WITHIN any insight dimension — classification, sub-classification, indicator, indicator rule, confidence, severity, or state — because in both each insight is its own row and these are groupable scalar dimensions; in AssetDetails_ch_agg those same fields are per-asset arrays and cannot be grouped correctly. Use THIS cube when the breakdown is purely by insight dimensions with little or no asset attributes (e.g. "zombie assets by sub-classification", "breakdown of insights by severity"); use AssetDetails_ch when the same query also groups by or returns asset attributes such as provider, OS, region, or vendor (e.g. "violated insights by provider and severity"). For asset inventory with rolled-up insight arrays — one row per asset, insight fields used only for filtering — use AssetDetails_ch_agg. Time dimension: default to updated_at (insight sync time) scoped to the last 7 days from now (to the minute); if the user specifies a time range — for example "in the last 3 hours", "over the past 2 days", or "not in the last 3 days" — apply those constraints instead, as user-specified time always takes priority over the default.

cubes.name: AssetLocations
cubes.title: Asset Locations
cubes.description: Reference lookup cube mapping cloud provider region codes to human-readable location names and labels. One row per provider-region combination. Use for questions about available regions, region display labels, or provider listings. Supports filtering by provider, region code, and geographic location. Joined by other cubes to resolve region codes into display-friendly names. No measures - pure dimension table.

cubes.name: AssetProviderData
cubes.title: Asset Provider Data
cubes.description: Provider-data comparison cube combining raw provider-specific rows with a synthetic common row derived from aggregated asset data for each asset. Grain is one row per asset-provider-source record, plus one additional common row per asset that represents the merged asset view. Each row exposes provider-reported attributes such as provider identity, source table, raw JSON payload, sync time, name, OS and version, vendor, model, serial number, IP or MAC addresses, location, tags, and provider-specific first or last seen timestamps. Use this cube when a query needs provider-level differences or raw provider payloads, for example "compare device names across providers", "show raw provider JSON for this asset", "find which provider last saw an asset", or "review OS and serial mismatches between common and provider rows". Prefer this cube over broader asset cube when the question is specifically about per-provider provenance, disagreement, or raw source data.

cubes.name: AssetProviderDataAttrIndex
cubes.title: Asset Provider Data Attr Index
cubes.description: Flattened attribute search index over provider raw JSON. Grain is one row per distinct (account, provider, source_table, json_path, value) tuple — deduplicated, so a value shared by many assets collapses to a single row (asset identity is intentionally not part of the grain). Each row exposes the JSON path, its original ClickHouse datatype, and the value cast to String. Use this cube to power attribute search and value autocomplete, for example "list the distinct json paths a provider reports", "suggest values for json_path 'Architecture'", or "find paths whose name contains 'launch'". Backed by ngrams(3) full-text indexes on provider, source_table and json_path, so substring search on those columns is granule-accelerated. The columns form a cascading drill-down hierarchy — provider → source_table → json_path → value — so narrow filters left-to-right (pick a provider, then a source_table, then a json_path) before suggesting values. For per-asset raw payloads or provider provenance use AssetProviderData instead; this cube is a distinct-attribute catalog, not a per-asset table.

cubes.name: AssetSource
cubes.title: Asset Sources
cubes.description: Lookup table of all discovery sources and providers in the asset platform. One row per unique source. Use for questions like 'what sources exist', 'list all providers', or 'show available discovery sources'. Supports filtering and grouping by source name or display label. Joined by asset cubes to resolve source identifiers to user-friendly labels.

cubes.name: AssetSubClassifications
cubes.title: Asset Sub Classifications
cubes.description: Lookup table mapping insight sub-classification codes to display labels, with one row per sub-classification. Sub-classifications use a "parent/child" path hierarchy across three types - zombie (e.g., "zombie/stale_device" -> "Stale Device"), compliance (e.g., "compliance/missing_patch" -> "Missing Patch"), and ghost (e.g., "ghost/discovery_gap" -> "Discovery Gap"). Use for questions about available sub-classifications, populating filter dropdowns, or resolving codes to friendly names. Supports filtering by zombie, compliance, and ghost insight types via segments. Joined by other asset cubes for sub-classification lookups - contains no measures. Example queries: "what sub-classifications exist", "list all zombie sub-types", "show compliance insight categories".

cubes.name: AssetSuperCategories
cubes.title: Asset Super Categories
cubes.description: Static lookup table enumerating top-level asset categories (Devices, Network, Services, Unverified). One row per category. Each represents a high-level grouping: "Devices" covers servers, workstations, laptops, IP phones, media devices, and power devices; "Network" covers routers, switches, firewalls, gateways, load balancers, subnets, and wireless controllers; "Services" covers DNS servers, storage, cloud services, and SaaS resources; "Unverified" covers ghost assets detected by one source but not confirmed by another. Use for questions like "what categories exist" or "list top-level asset groupings". Supports populating category filter dropdowns and validating category values. Example queries: "what categories exist", "list top-level asset groupings", "how many network devices do I have", "show all unverified assets".

cubes.name: AssetTypeLabels
cubes.title: Types
cubes.description: Dimension-only lookup cube mapping raw cloud resource type identifiers to human-readable display names, one row per resource type. Use for questions about what asset resource types exist, listing resource types, populating resource type filter dropdowns, or resolving resource codes to friendly names. Supports filtering by resource type code or display name. Use when asking "what asset resource types exist", "list resource types", or "show available resource types".

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight Device Interface Agg Expanded
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes with network interface data. Each row represents one asset and exposes: (1) common asset fields -- name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insights -- insight types, indicator IDs, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys like insight_types_confidence_levels; and (3) network interface attributes -- interface details like VRF names, IP addresses, MAC addresses, etc. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH common asset attributes AND network interface attributes -- for example "show me assets with specific interface configurations", "list devices with their network interfaces", or "filter assets by interface properties". Do NOT use this cube for insight-only or asset-only queries where interface data is not needed; prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg for those cases.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight Device Interface Expanded
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes and network interface attributes. This non-aggregated version keeps insight rows at detailed grain, so one asset can produce multiple rows when multiple indicators/rules exist. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH asset/insight context AND interface-level fields such as interface name, VLANs, VRF, trunk status, link aggregation, switch/wireless info, or DHCP lease details. Example queries: "show active insights on assets connected to trunk interfaces", "list assets with failed registration insights and interface oper status down", or "find devices with specific VRF names and their insight indicators". Do NOT use this cube for provider raw attributes; use Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_Expanded or Asset_Insight_ProviderData_Expanded when provider-specific columns are required.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight Device Interface Provider Data Agg Expanded
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes with network interface data and raw provider discovery data. Each row represents one asset and exposes: (1) common asset fields -- name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insights -- insight types, indicator IDs, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys like insight_types_confidence_levels; (3) network interface attributes -- interface details like VRF names, IP addresses, MAC addresses, etc.; and (4) raw provider attributes -- per-provider name, categories, OS, vendor, model, serial number, IPs, MACs, location, last seen, tags, pd_standardized_json_attributes, and the full pd_raw_json blob. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH common asset attributes AND BOTH network interface AND provider-specific attributes -- for example "show me AWS EC2 instances with their network interfaces and VPC configurations", "list devices with interface and provider data", or "filter assets by both interface properties and provider attributes". Do NOT use this cube for queries where either interface or provider data is not needed; prefer simpler cube like AssetDetails_ch_agg for those cases.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight Device Interface Provider Data Expanded
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes, network interface attributes, and provider-specific raw attributes. This non-aggregated version keeps detailed insight rows, so one asset can produce multiple rows across indicators/rules and joined provider/interface records. Use this cube when a query needs the broadest field coverage across asset + insight + interface + provider domains in one result set. Example queries: "show unacknowledged high-severity insights for assets where interface is trunk and provider model matches X", "find assets with insight state active, provider tags containing Y, and interface VLAN Z", or "compare provider OS/version with interface telemetry for impacted assets". Do NOT use this cube for simple asset-only or insight-only analysis; prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg for better simplicity and performance.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_UserData_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight Device Interface Provider Data User Data Agg Expanded
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes with network interface data, raw provider discovery data, and per-user identity data. Each row represents one asset and exposes: (1) common asset fields -- name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insights -- insight types, indicator IDs, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys like insight_types_confidence_levels; (3) network interface attributes -- interface details like VRF names, IP addresses, MAC addresses, etc.; (4) raw provider attributes -- per-provider name, categories, OS, vendor, model, serial number, IPs, MACs, location, last seen, tags, pd_standardized_json_attributes, and the full pd_raw_json blob; and (5) user identity fields -- first/last name, login ID, email, provider, and per-action provider map for the most recent user who logged on in the last 7 days. Use this cube when a query needs asset + interface + provider + user domains together -- for example "show assets with VPC interface and provider data where a specific user recently logged on". Do NOT use this cube for queries where user, interface, or provider data is not needed; prefer simpler cubes for those cases.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_UserData_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight Device Interface Provider Data User Data Expanded
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes, network interface attributes, provider-specific raw attributes, and per-user identity data. Grain is one row per asset-insight combination. Use this cube when a query needs the broadest field coverage across asset + insight + interface + provider + user domains in one result set. Example queries: "show high-severity insights for assets where interface is trunk and logged-on user matches X", "find assets with active insight, provider tags containing Y, and interface VLAN Z with recent user logon". Do NOT use this cube for simple asset-only or insight-only analysis; prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg for better simplicity and performance.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_UserData_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight Device Interface User Data Agg Expanded

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_ProviderData_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight Provider Data Agg Expanded
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes with raw provider discovery data. Each row represents one asset and exposes: (1) common asset fields -- name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insights -- insight types, indicator IDs, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys like insight_types_confidence_levels; and (3) raw provider attributes -- per-provider name, categories, OS, vendor, model, serial number, IPs, MACs, location, last seen, tags, pd_standardized_json_attributes, and the full pd_raw_json blob. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH common asset attributes (shared across all providers) AND provider-specific attributes that are only available from a particular source -- for example "show me all Jamf Pro assets where disk encryption is enabled", "list AWS EC2 instances with their instance type and IAM role from the provider", or "show AWS EC2 instances with their VPC ID and security groups". Do NOT use this cube for insight-only or asset-only queries where provider raw data is not needed; prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg for those cases.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_ProviderData_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight Provider Data Expanded
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes and provider-specific raw attributes. This non-aggregated version preserves detailed insight rows and provider-level columns such as pd_provider, pd_source_table, pd_ip_addresses, pd_mac_addresses, pd_tags, pd_standardized_json_attributes, and pd_raw_json. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH common asset/insight fields AND provider payload context, for example "show active compliance insights with provider-reported model and serial", "find assets by provider tag values and insight indicator", or "inspect provider JSON for assets with critical findings". Do NOT use this cube for interface-focused analysis; use Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_Expanded or Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_Expanded when interface fields are required.

cubes.title: Asset Insight User Data Expanded

cubes.name: DeviceInterface
cubes.title: Device Interface
cubes.description: Network-interface cube enriched with asset context for the first attached device. Grain is one row per latest interface record for a device and interface name. Each row exposes interface-level details such as classification, description, sync time, IP and MAC assignments, admin or oper state, speed, VLANs, trunk and aggregation status, VRF metadata, switch or wireless connectivity details, DHCP lease information, IP-space mappings, and attached-device tuples, plus resolved fields for the connected asset such as name, vendor, model, OS, provider, region, status, and taxonomy category. Use this cube when the question is about interface topology or connectivity with asset context, for example "which asset is connected to this port", "show interfaces with attached device details", "find trunk ports connected to inactive assets", or "review switch or wireless connectivity alongside the attached asset identity". Prefer this cube over broader asset cubes when interface-specific state or attached-device relationships are the primary focus.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled
cubes.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Rolled
cubes.description: IP address overlap detection results rolled up to one row per address CIDR per tenant, summarizing how many address blocks and subnets share the same IP range. Extends NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase. Use for questions about overlap counts per address, which IP spaces or providers are involved in overlaps, or filtering overlap summaries by provider or source. For per-object overlap details, use NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList instead.

cubes.name: NstarDnsActivity
cubes.title: Nstar DNS Activity
cubes.description: Deprecated — migrate to OnPremDnsActivityV1. Retained for backward compatibility only; removed on 2027-07-16. Raw DNS query activity from on-premises N-Star DNS appliances, with one row per individual DNS query event.

cubes.name: NstarLeaseActivity
cubes.title: Nstar Lease Activity
cubes.description: Deprecated — migrate to OnPremDhcpLeaseActivityV1. Retained for backward compatibility only; removed on 2027-07-16. DHCP lease activity from on-premises DNS/DHCP appliances with one row per lease event.

meta.ai_context: ⚠️ NIOS DHCP lease logs are not queryable via this cube. This is a known limitation. Instead of telling the user that there are no lease records for a NIOS DHCP server, you should make clear that this is a known limitation.

cubes.name: SecurityActionAssets
cubes.title: Security Action Assets
cubes.description: Per-asset detail for security actions, one row per asset per security action. Terminology: "insight" is the user-facing alias for "security action" in the IQ Threat Defense UI — treat the two terms as synonyms. Each record describes a device including network identifiers (IP, MAC, hostname), threat indicators on the asset, associated users, event counts, verification status, risk flag, provider/region, ranking, and first/last detection timeline. Scope: rows created in the last 30 days where the parent security action has visible=true. Use this cube to check all assets involved for a particular security action, or to see all risky assets across security actions — it's suggested to use it with securityActionDisplayId in the filter when scoping to a single security action. For security action-level summaries use SecurityActionSummaryView; for indicator-level drill-downs use SecurityActionIndicators.

cubes.name: SecurityActionIndicators
cubes.title: Security Action Indicators
cubes.description: Threat indicator detail for security actions, one row per indicator per security action. Terminology: "insight" is the user-facing alias for "security action" in the IQ Threat Defense UI — treat the two terms as synonyms. Each record describes an IOC (domain, IP, URL) including threat level, confidence rating, threat actor, event volume, affected verified/unverified assets, associated users, enforcement action status, and first/last detection timeline. Scope: rows created in the last 30 days where the parent security action has visible=true. Use this cube to check all threat indicators involved for a particular security action, or to see all high-severity / high-confidence indicators across security actions — it's suggested to use it with securityActionDisplayId in the filter when scoping to a single security action. For security action-level summaries use SecurityActionSummaryView; for asset-level drill-downs use SecurityActionAssets.

cubes.name: SecurityActionSummaryView
cubes.title: Security Action Summary View
cubes.description: Top-level security action inventory — one row per security action. Terminology: "insight" is the user-facing name for a security action in the IQ Threat Defense UI — treat "insight" and "security action" as synonyms, so questions like "how many insights" or "total number of insights" map to this cube's count measure. Scope: rows where visible=true and insight_created_at is within the last 30 days. Use for listing and filtering security actions, ranking by severity or time-saved, and reporting totals. Key fields: name, description, severity (Low/Medium/High/Critical), currentStatus (Needs Review, In Progress, Resolved, Closed, Expired, Reopened, Accepted Risk, False Positive), impact counts (totalEvents, totalIndicators, totalVerifiedAssets, totalUnverifiedAssets, totalUsers), effort metrics in seconds (manualTime, agentTime, timeSaved), threat context (tproperties, tclasses, threatActors), evaluation window (evaluationStartDate, evaluationEndDate), and derived expiringInDays (-1 expired, -2 not in warning window, 1-7 days remaining). Example questions: "list High severity security actions", "security actions currently In Progress", "security actions expiring in the next 7 days", "total time saved by automation". For per-security-action drill-downs use SecurityActionAssets / SecurityActionIndicators / SecurityActionRecommendations, joined on SecurityActionSummaryView.displayID ↔ SecurityActionAssets.securityActionDisplayId / SecurityActionIndicators.securityActionDisplayId / SecurityActionRecommendations.securityActionDisplayId.

cubes.name: ip_history
cubes.title: IP History
cubes.description: IP-history cube that reconstructs contiguous assignment windows for currently active asset and IP pairs. Grain is one row per asset, IP address, and contiguous time period, where gaps of at least one day start a new history segment. Each row exposes the asset CQID, name, resource type, categories, deployment context, the assigned IP address, and the start and end timestamps for that assignment interval. Use this cube when the question is about IP ownership over time, for example "when did this asset have this IP", "which assets used a given IP", "show IP changes for an asset", or "review the timeline of active IP assignments". Prefer this cube over broader asset cubes when temporal IP assignment history is the primary focus.

full.name: AssetCategories
full.title: Asset Categories
full.description: Lookup table of all asset type label. Type classify assets by type using snake_case IDs mapped to human-readable names - cloud (e.g., "virtual_machine" -> "Virtual Machine", "cloud_firewall" -> "Cloud Firewall", "dns_server" -> "DNS Server", "storage_bucket" -> "Storage Bucket"), network (e.g., "router" -> "Router", "switch" -> "Switch", "load_balancer" -> "Load Balancer"), and IoT/endpoint (e.g., "camera" -> "Camera", "printer" -> "Printer", "bare_metal_server" -> "Bare-Metal Server"). An asset can have multiple Types. Use this cube to list available categories and their display names. Example queries: "what types exist", "list all asset types", "show me all firewall assets", "how many virtual machines do I have", or populating a type filter dropdown.

full.name: AssetDetailsOnly
full.title: Asset Details Only
full.description: Asset-only inventory cube with one row per unique asset (no insight row expansion). Exposes common normalised asset attributes such as name, provider, region/location, OS/version, vendor/model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, taxonomy hierarchy, tags, lifecycle fields, and discovery status signals. Use this cube only for tag-introspection or asset-registry-lookup queries that do not enumerate assets by attribute, for example "find assets by tag key/value", "list all available tag keys", "count assets by provider", or "show devices by taxonomy type". Do NOT use this cube for general asset enumeration such as "list Windows servers", "show managed devices by region", or "find assets by OS" — use AssetDetails_ch_agg for those. Do NOT use this cube when the query requires insight-specific fields (indicator/state/severity/confidence) or provider/interface expanded raw attributes; use AssetDetails_ch_agg in that case. Time dimension: default to updated_at scoped to the last 7 days from now (to the minute); if the user specifies a time range — for example "in the last 3 hours", "over the past 2 days", or "not in the last 3 days" — apply those constraints instead, as user-specified time always takes priority over the default.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.account_id
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Account ID
dimensions.description: Internal tenant account identifier, automatically filtered by the platform's security context. Use when tenant-level filtering is needed. See cqid for the asset identifier.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.cqid
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only CQID
dimensions.description: Unique CloudQuery identifier for each asset/device. Use when filtering or looking up a specific asset by its ID (CQID).

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.composite_id
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Composite ID
dimensions.description: Composite key. Used internally for uniqueness. Rarely needed in user queries.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.category
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Category
dimensions.description: Individual asset category (unnested from array). Use when filtering or grouping by category such as "show assets by category", "filter by category X". One asset may appear in multiple categories.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.category_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Category label
dimensions.description: Human-readable display name for the asset category. Use this instead of raw category when displaying to users or when the user refers to categories by their friendly name.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.categories
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Categories
dimensions.description: All categories for an asset as a JSON array string. Use when you need the full list of categories per asset rather than one-per-row. Not for filtering, use "category" dimension instead.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.cidrs
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only CIDR
dimensions.description: Network CIDR blocks associated with the asset as a JSON array string. Use when asking about "network ranges", "subnets", or "CIDR blocks" of an asset.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.cloud_account_id
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Cloud Account ID
dimensions.description: The cloud provider account ID (e.g., AWS account ID, Azure subscription). Use when filtering by "cloud account", "AWS account", or grouping assets by their cloud account.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.context
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Context
dimensions.description: Contextual metadata about the asset source or discovery context.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.dhcp_fingerprint
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only DHCP Fingerprint
dimensions.description: DHCP fingerprint string used for device identification. Use when asking about "DHCP fingerprint", "device fingerprinting", or network-level device identification.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.discovery_host
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only OPHID
dimensions.description: Do not use for filtering or display. Display name of the on-premises discovery host/appliance that found this asset. Not the OPHID itself, see the "ophid" dimension for the actual On-Prem Host ID. Use when filtering or displaying by discovery host name.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.ip_address
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only IP Address
dimensions.description: Individual IP address of the asset (unnested from array). Use when filtering or searching by a specific IP address, e.g., "find asset with IP 10.0.0.1". One asset may have multiple IPs, producing multiple rows.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.ip_addresses
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only IP Addresses
dimensions.description: All IP addresses of the asset as a JSON array string. Use when you need the full list of IPs per asset. Not for filtering, use "ip_address" dimension instead.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.location
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Location
dimensions.description: Raw location string of the asset. Use "location_label" for a human-friendly version.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.location_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Location label
dimensions.description: Human-readable location derived from provider and region (e.g., "US East (N. Virginia)"). Falls back to region name or "Global". Use when asking "where is the asset located" or grouping by location.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.mac_address
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only MAC Address
dimensions.description: Individual MAC address of the asset (unnested from array). Use when filtering or searching by a specific MAC address. One asset may have multiple MACs.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.mac_addresses
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only MAC Addresses
dimensions.description: All MAC addresses of the asset as a JSON array string. Use when you need the full list of MACs per asset. Not for filtering, use "mac_address" dimension instead.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.model
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Model
dimensions.description: Hardware model of the asset/device (e.g., "Cisco ISR 4331"). Use when asking about "device model", "hardware model", or grouping by model.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.name
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Name
dimensions.description: Display name or hostname of the asset. Use when searching by name, e.g., "find asset named X", or when displaying asset details.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.ophid
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only OPHID
dimensions.description: On-Prem Host ID, the unique identifier of the on-premises host or appliance associated with this asset. Use when filtering by OPHID or looking up assets tied to a specific on-prem host.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.os
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Operating System
dimensions.description: Operating system name of the asset (e.g., "Windows 10", "Ubuntu 22.04", "IOS-XE"). Use when asking "what OS", "show assets by operating system", or filtering by OS.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.perspective_tag
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Perspective Tag
dimensions.description: Individual perspective tag (unnested). Use when filtering or grouping by a specific perspective tag. One asset may have multiple tags.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.perspective_tags
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Perspective Tags
dimensions.description: All perspective tags for the asset as a JSON array string. Use when you need the full list of perspective tags per asset.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.provider
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Provider
dimensions.description: Do not use for filtering or display. Primary discovery source or cloud provider (e.g., "aws", "azure", "gcp", "nios", "servicenow"). Use when asking "which provider", "show assets by provider", or filtering by cloud/discovery source. Use "provider_label" for display.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.provider_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Provider label
dimensions.description: Do not use for filtering or display. Human-readable provider name with proper casing (e.g., "AWS", "GCP", "Azure", "ServiceNow"). Use for display instead of raw provider value.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.providers_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only ProvidersLabel
dimensions.description: All providers/sources for this asset as a formatted array. Use when displaying the full list of sources that discovered this asset.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.providers_label_iterator
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only ProvidersLabel
dimensions.description: Each source/provider unnested into individual rows with display labels. An asset discovered by 3 providers produces 3 rows. Use when grouping or filtering by all sources. For raw values, use providers_iterator. For primary source only, use provider.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.providers_iterator
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Providers_iterator
dimensions.description: Each raw source/provider unnested into individual rows. Use "providers_label_iterator" instead for display-friendly names.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.provider_location_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Provider Location Label
dimensions.description: Alias for provider_region_label. Human-readable label combining provider and region.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.provider_region_label_old
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Provider Region Label
dimensions.description: Legacy format of provider+region label. Used internally by provider_region_label. Prefer "provider_region_label" instead.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.provider_region_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Region Label
dimensions.description: Human-readable region label (e.g., "AWS US East (N. Virginia)", "Unassigned"). Use when asking "which region", "show assets by region", or displaying region info. "Unknown" regions appear as "Unassigned".

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.provider_region
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Provider Region
dimensions.description: Raw provider region code (e.g., "us-east-1", "westus2"). Use "provider_region_label" for display-friendly version.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.provider_label_filter_based
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Provider label from filter
dimensions.description: Provider label derived from the reconciliation filter. Used internally by the reconciliation dimension. Not for direct user queries.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.reconciliation
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Reconciliation
dimensions.description: Cross-source reconciliation status for a given provider filter. Values: "Matching" (asset found in selected provider AND others), "Missing From X" (not in selected provider), "Only in X" (only in selected provider). Use when asking "which assets are missing from AWS" or "reconciliation report". Requires reconciliation_filter to be set.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.reconciliation_filter
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Reconciliation filter
dimensions.description: Filter dimension used to select which provider to reconcile against. Set this filter value to a provider name (e.g., "aws") to enable reconciliation analysis.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.region
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Region
dimensions.description: Raw cloud region code. Use "provider_region_label" for display-friendly region names.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.region_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Region Label
dimensions.description: Human-readable cloud region label (e.g., "US East (N. Virginia)"). Falls back to raw region or "Global". "Unknown" is replaced with "Unassigned".

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.secondary_providers
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Secondary Providers
dimensions.description: Do not use for filtering or display. Additional discovery sources beyond the primary provider, as a JSON array. Use when checking which other sources also discovered this asset.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.source_table
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Source Table
dimensions.description: Name of the internal source table that originated this asset record. Used for debugging data lineage.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.providers
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Providers
dimensions.description: All discovery sources/providers for this asset as a JSON array string. Use when you need the raw list of all sources. For filtering/grouping, use "providers_iterator" or "providers_label_iterator" instead.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.source_job_name
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Source Job Name
dimensions.description: Name of the discovery job that found this asset. Use when filtering by discovery job or debugging which job populated the asset.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.super_category
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Super Category
dimensions.description: Top-level classification of the asset (e.g., "compute", "network", "iot", "storage"). Use when asking "show assets by super category" or for high-level grouping. Use "super_category_label" for display.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.super_category_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Super Category Label
dimensions.description: Capitalized display name for super category (e.g., "Compute", "Network"). Use for user-facing display.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.system_tags
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only System tags
dimensions.description: System-assigned tags as a JSON object string. These are auto-generated tags, not user-defined. Use when querying system-level metadata tags.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.display_type
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Asset/Resource type
dimensions.description: Raw asset or resource type identifier in snake_case format (e.g., "aws_ec2_instances", "aws_s3_buckets"). These are internal type identifiers, not human-readable display names. Use when asking "what type of asset", "show asset types", or grouping by device/resource type.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.user_tags
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only User tags
dimensions.description: User-defined tags as a JSON object string with key-value pairs. Use when filtering or viewing custom tags applied by users.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.vendor
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Vendor
dimensions.description: Hardware or software vendor/manufacturer (e.g., "Cisco", "Dell", "Microsoft"). Use when asking "show assets by vendor", "which vendor", or filtering by manufacturer.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.created_at
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Created Time
dimensions.description: When the asset was first created/discovered. Use when filtering by creation date, e.g., "assets created in the last 30 days" or "assets created after January 2026".

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.updated_at
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Updated Time
dimensions.description: When the asset was last updated. Use when filtering by "recently updated assets" or sorting by last update time.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.deleted_at
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Delete Time
dimensions.description: When the asset was soft-deleted. Null means the asset is active (not deleted). Use segments "existing_assets" or "removed_assets" instead of filtering this directly.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.first_seen
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only First Seen Time
dimensions.description: When the asset was first observed on the network. Use when asking "when was this asset first seen" or filtering by first seen date.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.last_seen
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Last Seen Time
dimensions.description: When the asset was last observed on the network. Use when asking "when was this asset last seen", "stale assets not seen in 30 days", or filtering by last seen date.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.length_categories
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Length of categories array
dimensions.description: Count of categories assigned to the asset. Used internally with the "IS EXACTLY" operator for array matching. Can be used to find "assets with exactly N categories".

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.length_ip_addresses
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Length of ips array
dimensions.description: Count of IP addresses on the asset. Used internally for array matching. Can be used to find "assets with multiple IPs" or "assets with exactly 1 IP".

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.length_cidrs
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Length of cidrs array
dimensions.description: Count of CIDR blocks associated with the asset. Used internally for array matching.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.length_providers
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Length of Provider array
dimensions.description: Count of discovery sources for the asset. Use when asking "how many providers discovered this asset" or "assets found by multiple sources".

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.length_secondary_providers
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Length of secondary_providers array
dimensions.description: Count of secondary providers. Used internally for array matching.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.length_mac_addresses
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Length of mac_addresses array
dimensions.description: Count of MAC addresses on the asset. Used internally for array matching.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.combined_tags
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Combines both user_tags and system_tags in same order
dimensions.description: Merged JSON object of both user_tags and system_tags. Use when querying across all tags regardless of whether they are user-defined or system-generated. Filter by tag key name using "contains" operator.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.combined_tags_all_keys
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Distinct Keys from user tags and system_tags
dimensions.description: Distinct list of all tag key names across user and system tags as a JSON array. Use when asking "what tags are available", "list all tag keys", or populating a tag key dropdown. Query with ungrouped=true.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.combined_tags_values_for_a_key
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Distinct Values for a tag key
dimensions.description: Distinct values for a specific tag key, returned as a JSON array. Requires "combined_tags" filter set to the desired key name. Use when asking "what are the values for tag X" or populating a tag value dropdown. Query with ungrouped=true.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.device_ip_dotted
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only IPAddress
dimensions.description: Primary IP address of the device in dotted notation (e.g., "192.168.1.1"). Use when displaying a single IP for the device in tables or detail views.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.device_name
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only DeviceName
dimensions.description: Name or hostname of the network device. Use when searching or displaying the device name in discovery context.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.device_type
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only DeviceType
dimensions.description: Type classification of the network device (e.g., "Router", "Switch", "Firewall"). Use when asking "what type of device" or grouping by device type in discovery context.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.reachable_status
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only ReachedStatus
dimensions.description: Whether the device is reachable via network (e.g., "Success", "Failed"). Use when asking "is the device reachable", "unreachable devices", or checking network connectivity status.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.reachable_message
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only ReachedMessage
dimensions.description: Detailed message explaining the reachability status. Use when drilling down into why a device is unreachable.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.snmp_credential_status
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only SNMPCredentialStatus
dimensions.description: Status of the SNMP credential check (e.g., "Success", "Failed"). Use when asking "SNMP credential issues" or filtering by SNMP authentication status.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.snmp_credential_message
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only SNMPCredentialMessage
dimensions.description: Detailed message explaining the SNMP credential status. Use when debugging SNMP credential failures.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.snmp_collection_status
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only SNMPCollectionStatus
dimensions.description: Status of SNMP data collection (e.g., "Success", "Failed"). Use when asking "SNMP collection issues" or checking if SNMP data was successfully collected.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.snmp_collection_message
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only SNMPCollectionMessage
dimensions.description: Detailed message about SNMP collection status. Use when debugging SNMP collection failures.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.cli_credential_status
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only CLICredentialStatus
dimensions.description: Status of CLI (SSH/Telnet) credential validation. Use when checking CLI authentication status across devices.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.cli_credential_message
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only CLICredentialMessage
dimensions.description: Detailed message about CLI credential status. Use when debugging CLI access failures.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.finger_print_status
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only FingerPrintStatus
dimensions.description: Status of device fingerprinting (device type identification). Use when checking if device type was successfully identified.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.finger_print_message
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only FingerPrintMessage
dimensions.description: Detailed message about device fingerprinting status.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.sdn_collection_status
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only SDNCollectionStatus
dimensions.description: Status of SDN (Software Defined Networking) data collection. Use when checking SDN integration status.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.sdn_collection_message
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only SDNCollectionMessage
dimensions.description: Detailed message about SDN collection status.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.updated_time
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only LastUpdate
dimensions.description: When the device discovery status was last updated. Use when asking "when was this device last updated" or sorting devices by most recent update.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.device_first_occurrence_time
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only FirstSeen
dimensions.description: When this device was first discovered on the network. Use when asking "when was this device first found" or filtering by discovery date.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.last_action
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only LastAction
dimensions.description: Most recent action performed on or by the device (e.g., discovery scan, configuration change). Use when checking the last activity on a device.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.discovery_status_last_seen
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only DiscoveryLastSeen
dimensions.description: When the discovery service last observed this device. Use when asking "when was this device last seen by discovery" or finding stale/offline devices.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.app_infra_service_id
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only DiscoveryService
dimensions.description: Identifier of the discovery service/appliance that manages this device. Use when filtering by discovery service or finding devices managed by a specific service.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.overall_status
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only OverallStatus
dimensions.description: Overall health/discovery status of the device. Use when asking "what is the device status" or filtering by overall health.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.snmp_collection_enabled
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only SNMPCollectionEnabled
dimensions.description: Whether SNMP collection is enabled for this device. Use when asking "is SNMP enabled", "devices with SNMP on/off".

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.cli_collection_enabled
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only CLICollectionEnabled
dimensions.description: Whether CLI (SSH/Telnet) collection is enabled for this device. Use when asking "is CLI collection enabled" or filtering by CLI status.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.sdn_collection_enabled
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only SDNCollectionEnabled
dimensions.description: Whether SDN collection is enabled for this device. Use when asking "is SDN enabled" on devices.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.device_assurance
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only Device Assurance

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.type_probability
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only TypeProbability
dimensions.description: Confidence category for device type identification: LOW (0-20), MEDIUM (21-74), HIGH (75-100). Use when asking "how confident is the device type", "show low-confidence devices", or grouping by type identification confidence.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_origins
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_origins
dimensions.description: All taxonomy origin classifications as a JSON array (e.g., ["cloud", "on-prem"]). Use when you need the full list of origins per asset.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_origin
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_origin
dimensions.description: Individual taxonomy origin (unnested). Values like "cloud", "on-prem". Use when grouping or filtering by origin, e.g., "show cloud vs on-prem assets".

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_resource_types
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_resource_types
dimensions.description: All taxonomy resource type classifications as a JSON array. Use when you need the full list of resource types per asset.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_resource_type
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_resource_type
dimensions.description: Individual taxonomy resource type (unnested). Use when grouping or filtering by resource type classification.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_super_categories
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_super_categories
dimensions.description: All taxonomy super category classifications as a JSON array (e.g., ["compute", "iot"]). Use when you need the full list.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_super_category
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_super_category
dimensions.description: Individual taxonomy super category (unnested). Use when grouping by taxonomy-based super category. Similar to super_category but from the taxonomy system.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_super_categories_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_super_categories_label
dimensions.description: Display-formatted taxonomy super categories as a JSON array (e.g., ["Compute", "IoT"]). Use for display purposes.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_super_category_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_super_category_label
dimensions.description: Display-formatted individual taxonomy super category (e.g., "IoT", "Compute"). Use for user-facing display when grouping by taxonomy super category.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_types
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_types
dimensions.description: All taxonomy type classifications as a JSON array. Most granular level of taxonomy. Use when you need the full list.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_type
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_type
dimensions.description: Individual taxonomy type (unnested). Most specific taxonomy classification. Use when grouping or filtering by the most detailed asset type in the taxonomy hierarchy.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_types_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_types_labels
dimensions.description: Display-formatted taxonomy types as a JSON array with dictionary lookups. "Uncategorized" for unknown types. Use for display.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_type_label
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_type_label
dimensions.description: Display-formatted individual taxonomy type with dictionary lookup. Falls back to raw value or "Uncategorized". Use for user-facing display.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.taxonomy_path
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only taxonomy_path
dimensions.description: Full taxonomy hierarchy path as a JSON array of "origin/resource_type/super_category/type" strings (e.g., ["cloud/infrastructure/compute/virtual_machine"]). Use when displaying the complete taxonomy hierarchy or for hierarchical grouping.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.os_type
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only OSType
dimensions.description: Type/family of operating system (e.g., "IOS-XE", "Windows", "Linux"). Use when grouping by OS family or filtering by OS type.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.os_version
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only OSVersion
dimensions.description: Specific version of the operating system (e.g., "17.3.4", "22.04"). Use when filtering by exact OS version or checking for outdated versions.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.serial_number
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only SerialNumber
dimensions.description: Hardware serial number of the device. Use when looking up a specific device by serial number.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.os_build
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only OSBuild
dimensions.description: Build number or identifier of the operating system (e.g., "22H2", "19045.3086"). Use when filtering by specific OS build or identifying patch levels.

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.parent_container_id
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only ParentContainerId

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.device_support
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only DeviceSupport

dimensions.name: AssetDetailsOnly.os_eos
dimensions.title: Asset Details Only OSEos
dimensions.description: Date when the OS version reaches End of Support (vendor stops providing updates). Use when asking "which assets are past end of support", "EoS dates", or identifying unsupported OS versions.
